content.prompt: In the diagram, calculate the exact value of $x$ so that $DE$ divides $\triangle ABC$ into two regions of equal area.

spec.description: Right triangleABC withAC18cm,BC10cm;D liesonAC,EonAB,DEperpendicularAC, source two right-angle marks retained. Dlocation schematic, no equal-area answer marks.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original given geometry/dimensions and shaded mathematical region; no calculated answers.

answer.worked:
The whole triangle has area $\tfrac12\times18\times10=90\text{ cm}^2$, so ADE has area 45. The two right triangles share angle A, so their corresponding height-to-base ratios are equal: $\frac{DE}{x}=\frac{10}{18}$.
$$\begin{aligned}DE&=\frac{5x}{9}\\45&=\frac12x\times\frac{5x}{9}\\x^2&=162\\x&=9\sqrt2\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}$$
Take the positive root because x is a length.
